title: Serve Runtime Sprint 23 Ops Digest
content:
Sprint 23 — Ops digest and standup notes (kernels, KV cache, batching)

Overview:
- Purpose: weekly capture of operational changes, perf experiments, blockers, and rollout decisions related to kernel optimizations, KV cache, and batching heuristics.
- Context: this sprint focused on landing the new fused-attention kernel prototype, iterating on KV prefix caching, and testing dynamic batch size selection in the router.

Attendees:
- Asha (notes), Miguel (kernels), Ravi (kv-cache), Lena (batching), Jun (SRE), Priya (observability, joined for canary review)

High-level status:
- Kernels: prototype fused-attn kernel merged to canary branch (PR #842). Microbench shows 12–16% lower p50 on long-seq workloads (seq_len 2k–4k) but 4% regression on short-seq p50 for small models.
- KV Cache: new prefix prefetch heuristic rolled to beta. Hit rate improved from ~62% -> 78% for the sampled customer workload set; tail latency for cache misses slightly worse on cold starts.
- Batching: dynamic batcher rollout to dedicated pool A completed; throughput up ~18% and p95 latency within SLO for 95% of traffic. Some jobs still show oscillation when request rate spikes >1.2x baseline.

Details — Kernels:
- What landed: fused-attn-vectorized (canary) — reduces memory copies and combines softmax+dropout ops. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Benchmarks:
  - Long seq (2k): p50 340ms -> 295ms (13% improvement), p95 540ms -> 495ms (8% improvement)
  - Short seq (128): p50 12ms -> 12.5ms (4% regression)
- Root cause of short-seq regression: vectorized code path increases per-call setup overhead for small token counts. Miguel will add a fast-path check to bypass fused kernel for seq<=256.
- Next steps: add perf guard that selects kernel based on sequence length histogram; experiment with JIT-tuning flags to reduce small-seq overhead. Owner: Miguel. Due: 2026-03-18.

Details — KV Cache (prefix prefetching):
- Experiment: proactive prefix prefetch on model variants with stable routing (customers with >=10k daily requests). Implemented as an async background pull with backoff.
- Results from 48h beta: average hit rate 78% (was 62%), token-cost reduction estimated 11% for the sample set. Cold start miss penalty increased median latency for first request by ~18ms.
- Observability: added kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.prefetches, kv_cache.evicts metrics. Grafana dash: "KV Cache Beta - Prefetch" (link in artifacts).
- Blocker: occasional burst of prefetch traffic overloaded a single LRU shard. Mitigation: rate-limit prefetch per-client and add jitter. Ravi to land shard-aware backpressure by 2026-03-15.

Details — Batching & Router heuristics:
- Dynamic batcher (alpha -> prod subset): router now adjusts max_batch_size per-model based on request rate and observed latency. Deployed to dedicated pool A.
- Observed: throughput +18%, cost-per-token down ~7% for that pool. However, under sudden spikes there is batch-size thrashing leading to p95 spikes.
- Short-term mitigation: add hysteresis to batch size changes (don't change more than 20% every 10s). Lena to implement and measure. Owner: Lena. Due: 2026-03-14.

Cross-cutting issues and decisions:
- Kernel selector policy: we'll implement a histogram-driven selector that chooses kernels by model, device, and recent seq_len distribution. Treat short sequences with a conservative fallback. Decision made 2026-03-11 in call.
- Prefetch safety: prefetch must be opt-in per-customer until backpressure/resilience issues are resolved. Default remains off for hosted tier.
- Canary rollout plan: new kernels + batcher changes will remain in canary for 1 week with 1% traffic, then 5% if stable, then increment. SRE triggers rollback on 2 consecutive p95 breaches.

Open blockers:
- PR #842 small-seq regression (owner: Miguel).
- KV prefetch shard pressure (owner: Ravi).
- Router batch thrash on spikes (owner: Lena).
- Missing tracing for inter-op cache misses across devices (owner: Jun).

Action items (owner, task, due):
- Miguel: add fast-path kernel bypass for seq<=256 and publish updated microbench. Due 2026-03-18.
- Ravi: implement sharded prefetch backpressure + jitter; add canary rate-limit config. Due 2026-03-15.
- Lena: add hysteresis to dynamic batcher; run stress test for 2x spike patterns. Due 2026-03-14.
- Jun: add tracing spans for cross-device KV misses and include counts in SLO alert rules. Due 2026-03-16.
- Priya: extend canary dashboard with rollout gating panels (SLOs, cost, error-rate). Due 2026-03-13.

Notes from the retro portion (fast, informal):
- What went well: close collaboration between kernels and batching teams allowed end-to-end wins; quick telemetry additions surfaced regressions fast.
- What to improve: more synthetic traffic variety in canaries (include rapid spike shapes), and tighter per-customer prefetch quotas.

Quick logs from daily standups (3 entries):
- 2026-03-09: Miguel: fused-attn build green; noticing small-seq overhead; adding benchmarks. Ravi: prefetch beta running at 1k clients. Lena: dynamic batcher stable on pool A. Jun: will add tracing.
- 2026-03-10: Miguel: fast-path sketch complete locally. Ravi: observed shard hot-spot, experimenting with per-shard token caps. Lena: saw batch thrash on synthetic 1.5x traffic spike.
- 2026-03-11: Decision call: canary sequencing and gating rules agreed. Owners assigned.

Misc notes / questions to follow up:
- Are we confident the prefetch model generalizes beyond sampled customers? Need broader A/B sample. (Action: Ravi to set up 7-day A/B run with 50 additional customers; start 2026-03-16)
- Should we expose a customer opt-in flag in hosted API console? Product input needed. (Asha to sync with product next week.)

Appendix — quick links and artifacts:
- Kernels PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- KV prefetch Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/RT-527-kv-cache-prefetch
- Canary dashboard: confluence://pages/SRV-ops-sprint-23

End of digest.
